clue.text: Enemy having been released from prison on many occasions

parts.note: time is proverbially the enemy, as in 'time, the old enemy'
a released prisoner is out after doing time, so the phrase reads as after time

explanation.surface: A foe who keeps getting out of jail again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'do time' is to serve a prison sentence, so someone released has come out after time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for repeatedly, again and again.

clue.text: Storm created by English politician in trial

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the word for trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An English MP being tried causes uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent windstorm, also a title of a Shakespeare play.

clue.text: Villain's crimes sorted out by diligent social worker

indicators.note: sorted out means the letters of crimes are rearranged

parts.note: the ant is a hard-working social insect, proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer's offences are dealt with by a dedicated welfare officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' looks like a welfare job; it is an insect living in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or rogue.

clue.text: Noah's final pair was taken aboard in flood

indicators.note: taken aboard means the word was goes inside them, as on to a ship
final pair says to take the last two letters of Noah

explanation.surface: Noah's last two animals are loaded on the ark during the deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered or overflowing with water.

clue.text: Pleasant occasion is introduction to extremely formal work

parts.note: a treat is an enjoyable event
taken as written

indicators.note: introduction to means the first letter of extremely

explanation.surface: A nice event becomes very formal at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: A systematic written discourse on a subject.

clue.text: Tease a lord, being humorously rude

parts.note: to rib is to tease

explanation.surface: Mocking a peer with crude jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarsely or vulgarly funny.

clue.text: International currency having difficulties

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: A global currency is in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means beset by problems or facing censure.

clue.text: Chaps brought in by paper boss to edit

indicators.note: brought in by means the chaps go inside the boss

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a newspaper's boss
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor recruits staff to revise copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct and improve a text.

clue.text: Tin god's temptations

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A false idol's lures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin god' looks like a phrase for a petty tyrant; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: Traps or lures that catch the unwary.

clue.text: Motorway investment is a blunder

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, written MI in crosswords
a stake is money put into a venture

explanation.surface: Putting money into a motorway turns out to be an error.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name an error or slip made through bad judgement.

clue.text: Very cold north is okay for bird

parts.note: bitter weather is very cold

explanation.surface: Freezing northern weather is said to suit a certain bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading heron of reedbeds, known for its booming call, is one species of bird.

clue.text: Terminal connection is a beastly hole

definitions.meaning: an electrical plug's ground terminal connects to this
a fox's or badger's burrow has this name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' means belonging to a beast, not nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an electrical ground connection and a wild animal's den.

clue.text: Unreasonable demand coming from oriental lord, erratically

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An eastern nobleman makes unpredictable and excessive requests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erratically' looks like an anagram signal but only supplies its first two letters to the run.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a request that is very hard or unfair to fulfil.

clue.text: The reverse of skill with poetry makes one cross

indicators.note: the reverse of says the word for skill is read backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A poet whose craft runs backwards ends up annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective, angry, but it is a verb: to go across.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross something is to go from one side of it to the other.

clue.text: Current supply is brought by these carriers

definitions.text: Current supply is brought by these carriers

parts.words: Current supply is brought by these carriers
parts.note: electric current is carried by these charged particles, read as delivery workers

explanation.definitionFit: Electricity in a wire is a flow of negatively charged subatomic particles.

clue.text: Bishop to be taken in by idiot who runs religious community?

indicators.note: taken in by means the bishop and the verb go inside the word for idiot

parts.note: an ass is a fool
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to be gives the verb be

explanation.surface: A bishop is fooled by a simpleton who heads a convent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent of nuns is its mother superior, the female counterpart of an abbot.

clue.text: Cautioned about school activity

indicators.note: about means the letters of cautioned are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning is given about lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching and learning are what schools do.

clue.text: Real mess one gets black in

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the word for mess

parts.note: a tangle is a mess
I is the Roman numeral for one
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A true muddle that someone dark gets caught up in.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to be touched, hence concrete and actual.

clue.text: One looking after baby? It's very easy

definitions.meaning: a babysitter, someone minding a child
an easy catch or chance, a dead cert

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a child-minder and, in sporting slang, something simple to achieve.

clue.text: Plan school unit for printing article

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of measure
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A school arranges a printing course for an item.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline or framework, a diagrammatic scheme.

clue.text: Spooner's Lady Fortune? Ineffective type

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady
luck is fortune

explanation.surface: Lady Luck is presented as a hopeless character.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Fortune is Lady Luck; swapping D and L turns DAME LUCK into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a weak or disabled person, especially an official about to leave office.

clue.text: Yale's entrance requirement

parts.note: Yale reads as the university but is a lock brand; a key needs somewhere to go in

explanation.definitionFit: A Yale lock needs an opening for the key to be inserted.

clue.text: Such a lot of lies in the paper

definitions.text: Such a lot of lies in the paper

parts.words: Such a lot of lies in the paper
parts.note: a web of lies is a familiar idiom, and a soft paper shares the word

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a fabric of falsehoods shares its word with thin soft paper.

clue.text: Thwart poor actors beginning to try massive operatic work

parts.note: hams are overacting performers

indicators.note: beginning to says to take the first letter of try

parts.note: Wagner's Ring cycle is a vast four-opera work

explanation.surface: Bad performers prevent an attempt to stage an enormous opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ring, short for Der Ring des Nibelungen, is Wagner's opera cycle lasting about fifteen hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To cripple by cutting a tendon, hence to frustrate or hinder.

clue.text: Simpleton at university found study hard

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person
to be up is to be in residence at university

explanation.surface: A fool at college discovered that revision was tough.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go up to university and are 'up' while studying there.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for cramming or swotting.

clue.text: Like a wide vessel at sea, maybe

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A broad ship out on the ocean, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's beam is its width, so a broad-beamed boat is described this way.

clue.text: Keep in what sounds like second-rate class

indicators.note: what sounds like signals that the phrase is spoken

parts.note: B is second-rate, as in a B grade, and a set is a class grouped by ability

explanation.surface: Staying behind in what seems to be a lower stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Schools in Britain group pupils by ability into sets, so a B set is a second-tier class.
explanation.definitionFit: To surround or hem in on all sides.

clue.text: Gentle group seen in publications

indicators.note: in means one word sits inside the other

parts.note: mags is short for magazines
to have got something is to have seen or understood it

explanation.surface: A crowd of mild people appears in magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gentle' is an anglers' noun for a maggot used as bait, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers call a bait larva a gentle, so several of them are fly larvae.

clue.text: Code of honour in wilderness, something revered mostly

parts.note: the bush is wild uncleared country

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an idol is something worshipped

explanation.surface: A principled code found in the wild alongside an object of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the L from IDOL, leaving IDO.
explanation.definitionFit: The samurai's traditional ethical code of loyalty and honour.

clue.text: Bill set out unusually neat instruction on envelope

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck on a wall

indicators.note: set out means the letters of set are laid out afresh
unusually means the letters of neat are arranged in an odd order

explanation.surface: Bill arranged a strangely tidy direction on the envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' makes EST and 'unusually' makes ANTE from NEAT; the answer is French for 'remain until called for'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase written on mail asks the post office to hold it for collection.
